title: Affine Schemes and the Structure Sheaf

items.title: The underlying space of an affine spectrum
items.strategy: For every commutative unital ring A, including A = 0, take the already-developed prime spectrum with its Zariski topology and distinguished-open basis; the structure sheaf is constructed next.

items.title: The localization presheaf on distinguished opens
items.strategy: Put O(D(f)) = A_f on the distinguished-open basis and define restrictions through the universal property of localization.

items.title: Localization sections are independent of a distinguished-open presentation
items.strategy: Use localization universality for restrictions; convert an arbitrary distinguished cover of Spec(A_f) to a finite unit-ideal subcover, glue compatible fractions, and verify the basis sheaf axiom directly.

items.title: The localization construction extends to the structure sheaf on Spec A
items.strategy: Extend the preceding basis sheaf by locally representable germ families, verify gluing pointwise, and prove agreement on the basis and uniqueness by the sheaf axiom.

items.title: Sections and restrictions on distinguished opens of an affine scheme
items.strategy: Transport the basis construction to the extended sheaf to prove Gamma(D(f), O) is canonically A_f, with the canonical localization restriction when D(g) is contained in D(f).

items.title: The stalk of the affine structure sheaf at a prime is A_p
items.strategy: Compute the stalk over the cofinal distinguished neighborhoods of p and identify its filtered colimit with A_p by localization universality.

items.title: Spec A with its structure sheaf is a locally ringed space
items.strategy: Combine the stalk computation with the localness of A_p to establish the locally ringed condition point by point.

items.title: The residue field at a point of an affine scheme
items.strategy: Define kappa(p) as O_p modulo its maximal ideal, then use the stalk and local-localization identifications to record its canonical presentation as Frac(A/p).

items.title: Global functions on Spec A recover A
items.strategy: Specialize the distinguished-open section calculation to D(1) = Spec A, including the zero-ring case.

items.title: A principal localization identifies its spectrum with a distinguished open
items.strategy: Combine the established homeomorphism Spec(A_f) = D(f) with the section and stalk calculations to upgrade it to an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces.

items.title: Affine schemes and their coordinate rings
items.strategy: Define an affine scheme as a locally ringed space isomorphic to Spec A and identify its coordinate ring through the preceding global-sections theorem.

items.title: The map of affine spectra induced by a ring homomorphism
items.strategy: For phi : A to B, construct the contraction map Spec B to Spec A and its compatible maps on localized basic-open sections; localness is verified in the next lemma.

items.title: The stalk maps induced by a ring map are local
items.strategy: Identify the stalk map at q with A_(phi inverse q) to B_q and check that its inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal.

items.title: Affine schemes are contravariantly equivalent to commutative rings
items.strategy: Use global sections for one composite, and reconstruct any locally ringed morphism into an affine target from its global-ring map and the canonical localization maps for the other.

items.title: Affine-scheme isomorphisms are exactly coordinate-ring isomorphisms in reverse direction
items.strategy: Reflect isomorphisms through the preceding anti-equivalence.

items.title: Closed points of an affine scheme
items.strategy: Define closedness topologically and translate it on Spec A to maximal ideals using the established Zariski correspondence.

items.title: Classical k-points give closed points over an algebraically closed field
items.strategy: For a reduced finite-type k-algebra over algebraically closed k, apply the established maximal-ideal correspondence and explicitly distinguish these k-points from all scheme points.

items.title: Generic points of irreducible closed subsets
items.strategy: Define generic point by closure and identify the prime p as generic for V(p) in an affine spectrum.

items.title: Every irreducible closed subset of an affine spectrum has a unique generic point
items.strategy: Use the prime--irreducible-closed-subset correspondence for existence and the T0 property for uniqueness.

items.title: Reduced affine schemes
items.strategy: Define reducedness by a reduced coordinate ring and use the affine anti-equivalence to show it is independent of an affine presentation.

items.title: Integral affine schemes
items.strategy: Define integrality by a nonzero domain coordinate ring and prove the equivalent nonempty, reduced, irreducible affine criterion.

items.title: An affine nilpotent thickening
items.strategy: For a nilpotent ideal I in A, define the affine map Spec(A/I) to Spec A and prove its underlying map is a homeomorphism although the structure sheaves may differ.

items.title: The functor of points of an affine scheme
items.strategy: Define h_X(R) = Hom_Sch(Spec R, X), covariantly in commutative test rings, and identify h_Spec A(R) with Hom_CRing(A, R) by the affine anti-equivalence.

items.title: An affine scheme is determined by its functor of points
items.strategy: Apply Yoneda to the representable point functors and translate the resulting natural isomorphism into an affine-scheme isomorphism.

items.title: The affine scheme of dual numbers
items.strategy: Define D_k = Spec(k[epsilon]/(epsilon squared)) as the first infinitesimal test scheme; its local calculation belongs to the companion page.

items.title: Every distinguished open of an affine spectrum is quasi-compact
items.strategy: Identify D(f) with Spec(A_f) as a locally ringed space and transfer quasi-compactness from the prime-spectrum theorem.

items.title: Every affine scheme is quasi-compact
items.strategy: Apply the preceding lemma to D(1) = Spec A, retaining the choice convention of the prime-spectrum compactness theorem.

items.title: Contravariance reverses coordinates and scheme points are not only classical points
items.strategy: Synthesize the anti-equivalence, residue-field convention, and closed/generic-point distinction without asserting a further theorem.

title: Affine Schemes and the Structure Sheaf — Examples

items.title: The spectrum of a field is a one-point affine scheme
items.strategy: Compute the sole prime, its local ring, residue field, and global sections from the field-localization formulas.

items.title: The zero ring has empty spectrum
items.strategy: Use the unital convention to show no prime ideal can be proper, then record the empty affine scheme and its zero global ring.

items.title: Spec Z has one generic point and closed prime-number points
items.strategy: Classify the primes of Z, then apply the closed-point and generic-point descriptions to separate (0) from (p).

items.title: Dual numbers give a one-point nonreduced affine scheme
items.strategy: Show (epsilon) is the only prime of k[epsilon]/(epsilon squared), while epsilon remains a nonzero nilpotent, and compute the residue field.

items.title: The spectrum of a product ring is a disjoint union
items.strategy: Classify prime ideals of A times B using complementary idempotents and match the localization sheaves to obtain Spec(A times B) isomorphic to Spec A disjoint union Spec B.

items.title: A basic open of the affine line is affine
items.strategy: For A1_k = Spec(k[t]), calculate D(t) as Spec(k[t,t inverse]) through the principal-localization open immersion.

items.title: The underlying topological space does not determine a scheme
items.strategy: Compare Spec k with the dual-numbers spectrum: both have one point, but their local rings and reducedness differ.

items.title: Relative points of the affine line are elements of a test k-algebra
items.strategy: For a specified k-algebra R, use the polynomial universal property to identify Hom_k-Alg(k[t], R) with R; via affine anti-equivalence these are maps Spec R to A1_k over Spec k.

items.title: A nonclosed scheme point need not be a k-valued coordinate
items.strategy: Use the generic point (0) of Spec(k[t]): its residue field is k(t), so it is not evaluation at an element of k.
